page.title: Dash Cam with Parking Mode: The Set to Buy and the Cutoff to Pick (2026)
page.h1: Dash cam with parking mode: the hardwired set and the cutoff voltage to pick
page.desc: Which dash cam parking mode set to buy (Viofo A229 Pro or A229 Plus with the HK4 hardwire kit, or the Thinkware U3000 radar) and which HK4 cutoff suits each type of car battery.
page.answer: Short answer. A dash cam with parking mode needs a hardwire kit: the Viofo A229 Pro with the HK4 hardwire kit is the best set for most cars, drawing 4.84 W parked. HK4 cutoffs read ±0.3 V, so pick 12.4 V on AGM or start-stop batteries; for days parked, Thinkware U3000 radar draws 0.20 W.

page.after:
What the differences mean

All draws are rcg530's DashCamTalk measurements with front and rear cameras running, in each camera's standby-for-event parking mode. Amps assume a resting battery at 12.6 V.

  • A229 Pro: 4.84 W ÷ 12.6 V = 0.38 A, × 12 h = 4.6 Ah per night.
  • A229 Plus: 4.23 W ÷ 12.6 V = 0.34 A, × 12 h = 4.0 Ah, which is 13% less than the Pro (4.23 ÷ 4.84 = 0.87).
  • Thinkware U3000 radar: 0.20 W ÷ 12.6 V = 0.016 A, × 48 h = 0.76 Ah over a weekend. The A229 Pro uses 0.38 × 48 = 18.4 Ah in the same time, about 24 times as much.
  • Dropping the rear camera lowers the A229 Pro's draw to 3.37 W (rcg530, 1CH). That saves 1.47 W, but you lose the rear view.
Your situationPick
Parked overnight at home or through a workday, and you want the most detail at the frontA229 Pro set
Same parking pattern, lower budget, 2K is enoughA229 Plus set
Car sits two days or more at a timeThinkware U3000 with radar parking
EV with a small 12 V accessory batteryA separate dash-cam battery pack, as BlackboxMyCar advises (see below)

{kit:kit-a229-pro-hardwired} is the set for most drivers. VIOFO's A229 Pro records 4K at the front and keeps the 15 seconds before an impact once the HK4 is wired in. This Amazon SKU includes the HK4 and an 8-piece fuse-tap set, and it cost less than buying the camera and the fuse-tap HK4 separately on 2026-11-14.

{kit:kit-a229-plus-hardwired} uses the same HK4 kit and the same parking modes, with 2K at both ends. It draws 0.61 W less than the Pro while parked.

The cutoff setting that protects your battery

The HK4 has a slide switch with four cutoffs: 11.8, 12.0, 12.2 and 12.4 V. VIOFO's support center says its kits detect voltage with about 0.3 V of tolerance. In the worst case, a kit set to 11.8 V can keep recording until the battery is at 11.5 V. Nexar suggests a cutoff for each battery type. Subtracting the 0.3 V from each HK4 setting gives the setting to use:

12 V batteryNexar's suggested cutoffHK4 settingWorst-case stop (setting − 0.3 V)
Standard lead-acid11.8 V12.2 V11.9 V
AGM12.0 V12.4 V12.1 V
Start-stop (EFB or AGM)12.0–12.2 V12.4 V12.1 V
EV 12 V lithium auxiliary12.2 Vnone: 12.4 − 0.3 = 12.1 V is below Nexar's 12.2 Vuse a battery pack

VIOFO calls 12.4 V its safest setting. If the battery still runs low, VIOFO suggests also setting a parking timer of about 2 hours. For EVs, BlackboxMyCar reports that a Tesla Model X owner got about 4 hours of parking recording from a BlackVue DR750S 1-CH with the cutoff at 12.0 V. It also says the Power Magic Pro and the splicing method do not work on the Model 3, which has no fuse box to hardwire into, and it recommends a separate dash-cam battery pack for EVs.

Wiring matters too. VIOFO's troubleshooting page says that if the yellow ACC wire goes to a constant-power fuse, the camera never switches into parking mode. The red wire goes to a constant fuse, the yellow to a switched one, and the black to ground.

Not recommended

  • The HK4 listing without fuse taps, unless you already own them. VIOFO's own HK4 page says 'Fuse Tap is not included'. Without a tap that matches your fuse box (ATO, Mini, Micro2 or Mini Low Profile), you can't finish the install with what you bought. Both sets above include the taps.
  • The HK6 for an A229. VIOFO says its days-long Hybrid Parking needs the HK6, and its parking-mode guide offers the Hybrid Parking HK6 kits for the A329S series and the A149 Pro. VIOFO lists the HK4 for the A229 Plus and Pro.
  • The HK3. It is the mini-USB kit for the A119 V3 and A129 cameras. The A229 has a Type-C port.
  • The 12 V socket alone. VIOFO lists the A229 Pro's parking modes as working with the HK4. Once the socket switches off with the ignition, there is no parking recording.
